Testing 
 
 Testing helps you write and maintain working Astro code. Astro supports many popular tools for unit tests, component tests, and end-to-end tests including Jest, Mocha, Jasmine,
Cypress 
 and
Playwright 
 . You can even install framework-specific testing libraries such as React Testing Library to test your UI framework components.
 
 Testing frameworks allow you to state
 assertions
 or
 expectations
 about how your code should behave in specific situations, then compare these to the actual behavior of your current code.
Unit and integration tests 
Section titled “Unit and integration tests” 
Vitest 
Section titled “Vitest” 
 A Vite-native unit test framework with ESM, TypeScript and JSX support powered by esbuild.
 
 Use Astro’s
 getViteConfig()
 helper in your
vitest.config.ts configuration file 
 vitest.config.ts
 configuration file
 to set up Vitest with your Astro project’s settings:
vitest.config.ts 
 vitest.config.ts
 ///   import { getViteConfig } from 'astro/config'; export default getViteConfig({ test: { // Vitest configuration options }, });
Copy to clipboard 
 
 By default,
 getViteConfig()
 will try to load an Astro config file in your project and apply it to the test environment. As of Astro 4.8, if you need to customize the Astro configuration applied in your tests, pass a second argument to
 getViteConfig()
 :
 
 export default getViteConfig( { test: { /* Vitest configuration options */ } }, { site: 'https://example.com/', trailingSlash: 'always', }, );
Copy to clipboard 
 
 See the
Astro + Vitest starter template 
 on GitHub.
Vitest and Container API 
Section titled “Vitest and Container API” 
 
 Added in:
 astro@4.9.0
 
 You can natively test Astro components using the
container API 
 . First, setup
vitest as explained above 
 vitest
 as explained above
 , then create a
 .test.js
 file to test your component:
example.test.js 
 example.test.js
 
 import { experimental_AstroContainer as AstroContainer } from 'astro/container'; import { expect, test } from 'vitest'; import Card from '../src/components/Card.astro'; test('Card with slots', async () => { const container = await AstroContainer.create(); const result = await container.renderToString(Card, { slots: { default: 'Card content', }, }); expect(result).toContain('This is a card'); expect(result).toContain('Card content'); });
Copy to clipboard 
End-to-end tests 
Section titled “End-to-end tests” 
Playwright 
Section titled “Playwright” 
 Playwright is an end-to-end testing framework for modern web apps. Use the Playwright API in JavaScript or TypeScript to test your Astro code on all modern rendering engines including Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox.
Installation 
Section titled “Installation” 
 
 You can get started and run your tests using the
VS Code Extension 
 .
 Alternatively, you can install Playwright within your Astro project using the package manager of your choice. Follow the CLI steps to choose JavaScript/TypeScript, name your test folder, and add an optional GitHub Actions workflow.
 Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them.
 If you are using npm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npm init playwright@latest
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using pnpm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 pnpm create playwright
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using yarn:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 yarn create playwright
Copy to clipboard 
Create your first Playwright test 
Section titled “Create your first Playwright test” 
 Complete the following steps in order.
 
 First, Choose a page to test. This example will test the example page
 index.astro
 below.
src/pages/index.astro 
 src/pages/index.astro
 
 --- ---      Astro is awesome!          
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Finally, Create a new folder and add the following test file in
 src/test
 . Copy and paste the following test into the file to verify that the page meta information is correct. Update the value of the page
  
 to match the page you are testing.
src/test/index.spec.ts 
 src/test/index.spec.ts
 
 import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'; test('meta is correct', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto("http://localhost:4321/"); await expect(page).toHaveTitle('
 Astro is awesome!
 '); });
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Set a baseUrl: You can set
    - 'link "\"baseURL\": \"http://localhost:4321\""':
 "baseURL": "http://localhost:4321"
 in the
 playwright.config.ts
 configuration file to use
 page.goto("/")
 instead of
 page.goto("http://localhost:4321/")
 for a more convenient URL.
Running your Playwright tests 
Section titled “Running your Playwright tests” 
 You can run a single test or several tests at once, testing one or multiple browsers. By default, your test results will be shown in the terminal. Optionally, you can open the HTML Test Reporter to show a full report and filter test results.
 Complete the following steps in order.
 
 First, To run our test from the previous example using the command line, use the
 test
 command. Optionally, include the file name to run just the single test:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx playwright test index.spec.ts
Copy to clipboard 
 Finally, To see the full HTML Test Report, open it using the following command:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx playwright show-report
Copy to clipboard 
 As a helpful tip, Run your tests against your production code to more closely resemble your live, deployed site.
  - 'heading "Advanced: Launching a development web server during the tests" [level=5]'
  - 'link "Section titled “Advanced: Launching a development web server during the tests”"':
 
 You can also have Playwright start your server when you run your testing script by using the
webServer 
 webServer
 option in the Playwright configuration file.
 Here is an example of the configuration and commands required when using npm:
 Complete the following steps in order.
 
 First, Add a test script to your
 package.json
 file in the project root, such as
 "test:e2e": "playwright test"
 .
 
 Second, In
 playwright.config.ts
 , add the
 webServer
 object and update the command value to
 npm run preview
 .
playwright.config.ts 
 playwright.config.ts
 
 import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test'; export default defineConfig({ + webServer: { + command: '
 npm run preview
 ', + url: 'http://localhost:4321/', + timeout: 120 * 1000, + reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI, + }, use: { baseURL: 'http://localhost:4321/', }, });
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Finally, Run
 npm run build
 , then run
 npm run test:e2e
 to run the Playwright tests.
 More information about Playwright can be found in the links below:
 
 
Getting started with Playwright 
 
Use a development server 
Cypress 
Section titled “Cypress” 
 Cypress is a front-end testing tool built for the modern web. Cypress enables you to write end-to-end tests for your Astro site.
Installation 
Section titled “Installation” 
 You can install Cypress using the package manager of your choice. This will install Cypress locally as a dev dependency for your project.
 Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them.
 If you are using npm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npm install cypress --save-dev
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using pnpm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 pnpm add --save-dev cypress
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using yarn:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 yarn add cypress --dev
Copy to clipboard 
Configuration 
Section titled “Configuration” 
 
 In the root of your project, create a
 cypress.config.js
 file with the following content:
cypress.config.js 
 cypress.config.js
 import { defineConfig } from 'cypress' export default defineConfig({ e2e: { supportFile: false } })
Copy to clipboard 
Create your first Cypress test 
Section titled “Create your first Cypress test” 
 Complete the following steps in order.
 
 First, Choose a page to test. This example will test the example page
 index.astro
 below.
src/pages/index.astro 
 src/pages/index.astro
 
 --- ---      Astro is awesome!         Hello world from Astro     
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Finally, Create an
 index.cy.js
 file in the
 cypress/e2e
 folder. Use the following test in the file to verify that the page title and header are correct.
cypress/e2e/index.cy.js 
 cypress/e2e/index.cy.js
 it('titles are correct', () => { const page = cy.visit('http://localhost:4321'); page.get('title').should('have.text', 'Astro is awesome!') page.get('h1').should('have.text', 'Hello world from Astro'); });
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Set a baseUrl: You can set
    - 'link "\"baseUrl\": \"http://localhost:4321\""':
 "baseUrl": "http://localhost:4321"
 in the
 cypress.config.js
 configuration file to use
 cy.visit("/")
 instead of
 cy.visit("http://localhost:4321/")
 for a more convenient URL.
Running your Cypress tests 
Section titled “Running your Cypress tests” 
 Cypress can be run from the command line or from the Cypress App. The App provides a visual interface for running and debugging your tests.
 First, start the dev server so Cypress can access your live site.
 To run our test from the previous example using the command line, execute the following command:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx cypress run
Copy to clipboard 
 Alternatively, to run the test using the Cypress App, execute the following command:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx cypress open
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Once the Cypress App is launched, choose
 E2E Testing
 , then select the browser to be used to run tests.
 Once the test run is finished, you should see green check marks in the output confirming that your test passed:
Output from npx cypress run 
 Output from npx cypress run
 
 Running: index.cy.js (1 of 1) ✓ titles are correct (107ms) 1 passing (1s)
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Fail the test: To check that your test really does work, you can change the following line in the
 index.astro
 file:
src/pages/index.astro 
 src/pages/index.astro
   -  Hello world from Astro  +  Hello from Astro   
Copy to clipboard 
 Then run the test again. You should see a red “x” in the output confirming that your test failed.
Next steps 
Section titled “Next steps” 
 More information about Cypress can be found in the links below:
 
 
Introduction to Cypress 
 
Testing Your App 
NightwatchJS 
Section titled “NightwatchJS” 
 Nightwatch.js is a test automation framework with a powerful set of tools to write, run, and debug your tests across the web with built-in support for all major browsers and their mobile equivalents, as well as native mobile applications.
Installation 
Section titled “Installation” 
 You can install NightwatchJS within your Astro project using the package manager of your choice. Follow the CLI steps to choose JavaScript/TypeScript, name your test folder, and select whether or not to include component testing and testing on mobile browsers.
 Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them.
 If you are using npm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npm init nightwatch@latest
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using pnpm:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 pnpm create nightwatch
Copy to clipboard 
 If you are using yarn:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 yarn create nightwatch
Copy to clipboard 
Create your first Nightwatch test 
Section titled “Create your first Nightwatch test” 
 Complete the following steps in order.
 
 First, Choose a page to test. This example will test the example page
 index.astro
 below.
src/pages/index.astro 
 src/pages/index.astro
 
 --- ---      Astro is awesome!          
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Finally, Create a new folder
 src/test/
 and add the following test file:
src/test/index.js 
 src/test/index.js
 describe('Astro testing with Nightwatch', function () { before(browser => browser.navigateTo('http://localhost:4321/')); it("check that the title is correct", function (browser) { browser.assert.titleEquals('Astro is awesome!') }); after(browser => browser.end()); });
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Set a baseUrl: You can set
    - 'link "\"baseURL\": \"http://localhost:4321\""':
 "baseURL": "http://localhost:4321"
 in the
 nightwatch.conf.js
 configuration file to use
 browser.navigateTo("/")
 instead of
 browser.navigateTo("http://localhost:4321/")
 for a more convenient URL.
Running your NightwatchJS tests 
Section titled “Running your NightwatchJS tests” 
 You can run a single test or several tests at once, testing one or multiple browsers. By default, your test results will be shown in the terminal. Optionally, you can open the HTML Test Reporter to show a full report and filter test results.
 
 You can run the tests with the
NightwatchJS VSCode Extension 
 or using the CLI steps below:
 Complete the following steps in order.
 First, To run all tests, enter the following command in the terminal. Optionally, include the file name to run just the single test:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx nightwatch test/index.js
Copy to clipboard 
 
 Additionally, you can run the tests against a specific browser using the
 --environment
 or
 -e
 CLI argument. If you don’t have the relevant browser installed, Nightwatch will attempt to set it up for you using
Selenium Manager 
 :
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx nightwatch test/index.ts -e firefox
Copy to clipboard 
 Finally, To see the full HTML Test Report, open it using the following command:
Terminal window 
 Terminal window
 npx nightwatch test/index.ts --open
Copy to clipboard 
 As a helpful tip, Run your tests against your production code to more closely resemble your live, deployed site.
 More information about NightwatchJS can be found in the links below:
 
 
Intro to Nightwatch 
 
Testing with Nightwatch
